extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the GAP computer algebra system (mathematicians and programmers using GAP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GAP language features describing interval operations, boolean semantics, and list types/operations (syntax, semantics, mutation, copying, membership, comparison, and performance hints). Intended to be used when writing or reading GAP code that manipulates intervals, booleans, and lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inf (interval attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inf(x) Returns the infimum of the interval x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute operation returning the lower bound of an interval. (Listed under interval attributes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid (interval attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid(x) Returns the midpoint of the interval x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute operation returning the center of an interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbsoluteDiameter / Diameter (interval attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: AbsoluteDiameter(x) / Diameter(x) Returns the absolute diameter of the interval x, namely the difference Sup(x)-Inf(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the interval width; useful for measuring absolute uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: RelativeDiameter (interval attribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: RelativeDiameter(x) Returns diameter (Sup(x)-Inf(x))/AbsoluteValue(Min(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as a relative measure of interval size; source text is partially garbled but expresses relative diameter as ratio of absolute diameter to AbsoluteValue(Min(x)). Use with caution and consult full manual for canonical formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDisjoint (interval predicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDisjoint(x1, x2) Returns true if the two intervals x1, x2 are disjoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boolean predicate testing non-overlap of intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubset (interval predicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSubset(x1, x2) Returns true if the interval x1 contains x2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate testing containment (note phrasing: 'x1 contains x2'). Applicable to interval floats.

rubrics_metrics.name: IncreaseInterval (interval operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: IncreaseInterval(x, delta) Returns an interval with same midpoint as x but absolute diameter increased by delta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a wider interval by adding delta to absolute diameter while preserving midpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlowupInterval (interval operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: BlowupInterval(x, ratio) Returns an interval with same midpoint as x but relative diameter increased by ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scales the relative width of the interval around the same midpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: BisectInterval (interval operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: BisectInterval(x) Returns a list of two intervals whose union equals the interval x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Splits an interval into two subintervals (useful for subdivision algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean values and naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The two main boolean values are true and false. It is a convention that the name of a function that returns true or false according to the outcome starts with Is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boolean values appear in conditional expressions and as return values of filters. The convention helps identify predicate functions (Is*).

rubrics_metrics.name: fail (boolean-like variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: fail is used to indicate situations when an operation could not be performed for the given arguments, either because of shortcomings of the arguments or because of restrictions in the implementation or computability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: fail is an object distinct from every other object and for technical reasons is regarded as a boolean value, but it cannot be used with and/or/not and cannot appear in boolean lists. Example: Position returns fail when element not found.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBool (filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBool(obj) tests whether obj is true, false or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to determine whether an object is one of the boolean-like values (including fail). Examples shown in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality and inequality of booleans
rubrics_metrics.description: bool1 = bool2 ; bool1 <> bool2: The equality operator = evaluates to true if both boolean values are equal (both true, both false, or both fail). The inequality operator <> evaluates to true if the two boolean values are different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes <> is also called exclusive or in the text. Comparisons with objects of other types are allowed (they are never equal). Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of booleans
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordering of boolean values is defined by true < false < fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering is used for comparisons using <, <=, etc. For comparison with other GAP objects see Section 4.13. Example comparisons are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean operators applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The logical operators and, or, not are only applicable to true and false (not to fail).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a boolean operator is given an operand that is neither true nor false, an error is signalled.

rubrics_metrics.name: or operator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: bool1 or bool2 evaluates to true if at least one operand is true, and to false otherwise. Evaluation is short-circuited: or first evaluates bool1; if neither true nor false an error; if true returns true without evaluating bool2; if false evaluates bool2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-circuiting avoids evaluating expensive or error-causing second operands. or is associative and has lowest precedence among logical operators; logical ops have lower precedence than comparison operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: and operator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: bool1 and bool2 evaluates to true if both operands are true, and to false otherwise. Evaluation is short-circuited: and first evaluates bool1; if neither true nor false an error; if false returns false without evaluating bool2; if true evaluates bool2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: and is associative, can be applied to filters (fil1 and fil2 returns a filter testing both on an argument). Precedence: and has higher precedence than or but lower than not. Examples given including filter combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: not operator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: not bool returns true if the boolean value bool is false, and true otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual text contains a likely typo in the last clause; intended meaning is logical negation with higher precedence than and/or. An error is signalled if operand does not evaluate to true or false. Examples illustrate usage and precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: List literal syntax and mutability
rubrics_metrics.description: A list is written by writing elements between square brackets [, ], separated by commas. An empty list is [] . Each such constructed list is mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists can contain other lists. Mutable vs immutable lists discussed elsewhere (see 12.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsList
rubrics_metrics.description: IsList(obj) tests whether obj is a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate for checking list type. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDenseList
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDenseList(obj) returns true if the list has no holes (i.e., contains an element at every position up to its length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists may have holes created by leaving entries empty; holes at end are ignored. Examples demonstrate hole behavior and consequences when accessing an unassigned entry (break-loop).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsHomogeneousList
rubrics_metrics.description: IsHomogeneousList(obj) returns true if obj is a list and it is homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homogeneous = dense list whose elements lie in the same family. Empty list is homogeneous but not a collection; nonempty homogeneous list is a collection. Examples show true/false cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTable
rubrics_metrics.description: IsTable(obj) A table is a nonempty list of homogeneous lists which lie in the same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical example: matrices. Examples illustrate rectangular vs non-rectangular and homogeneity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRectangularTable
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRectangularTable(list) True when list is nonempty and its elements are homogeneous lists of the same family and the same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property used to recognize rectangular tables (matrices).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConstantTimeAccessList
rubrics_metrics.description: IsConstantTimeAccessList(list) Category indicating whether access to each element takes roughly the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied by IsList and IsInternalRep; strings, boolean lists, ranges, and internally represented plain lists are in this category. Other enumerators can lie in this category if they guarantee constant-time access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic list operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic operations: element access, assignment of elements, fetching length, test for a hole at given position, and unbinding an element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic operations are primitives from which other list operations are formulated. For internally represented lists, kernel methods for positive integer indices exist; for other lists or indices methods can be installed, permitting lazy/enumerated lists with space-time trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element access and special operation names
rubrics_metrics.description: \[\](list, ix) and related operations implement element access, IsBound\[\], \[\]:=(list,pos,ix), Unbind\[\](list,ix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special characters in operation names must be escaped with backslash in documentation. The [] notation list[ix] is equivalent and preferred; the symbolic operation form is useful when accessing the operation itself (for installing methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and origin
rubrics_metrics.description: list[ix] evaluates to the element at index ix; for built-in lists indexing is origin 1 (first element index 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list not built-in or ix not positive integer, method selection is invoked; if method selection fails or the index is unbound, an error is signalled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublist extraction with { }
rubrics_metrics.description: list{poss} returns a new list whose entries are list[poss[i]] for each i; poss need not be sorted and may contain duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unbound positions cause an error. Sublist extraction can be nested; concept of selector 'level' defines behavior for nested selectors and is implemented by ListElement/ListElements pseudo-code in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: List element assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: list[ix] := object assigns object to index ix in the mutable list, possibly enlarging the list if ix > Length(list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment changes the list in-place, so list must be mutable. Enlarging may create holes. Use Add to append to end. If index or list types are unsuitable, method selection is invoked and errors may be signalled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublist assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: list{poss} := objects assigns objects[i] to list[poss[i]] for each i; poss must be a dense list of positive integers and objects must be a dense list of same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nested sublist assignments follow the same 'level' semantics as extraction; pseudo-code ListAssignment/ListAssignments in manual defines precise behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add (list insertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add(list, obj[, pos]) adds obj to the mutable list: two-arg form appends at end; three-arg inserts at pos shifting later elements up by one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holes at/after pos are moved up and new holes created before pos if needed. Add returns nothing (side-effect only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove (list deletion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove(list[, pos]) removes an element: one-arg form removes last element and returns it (list must be non-empty); two-arg form removes element at pos and returns old value if bound, otherwise returns nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-arg form moves subsequent elements down one position and moves holes accordingly. Accessing/assigning the return value of two-arg Remove is only safe when a value is known to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: CopyListEntries (low-level copying)
rubrics_metrics.description: CopyListEntries(fromlst, fromind, fromstep, tolst, toind, tostep, n) copies n elements from fromlst to tolst with given start indices and steps; fromlst and tolst must be plain lists; unbound positions are copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used internally by Add and Remove implementations; fromstep and tostep may be negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Append (in-place concatenation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Append(list1, list2) adds elements of list2 to the end of mutable list1; list2 may contain holes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Append modifies its first argument and returns nothing. Use Concatenation to create a new list leaving arguments unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBound (for list index)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBound(list[, n]) returns true if list has an element at index n, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: list must be a list or an object with an IsBound[] method installed. IsBound and Unbind are special in that they do not evaluate their argument (so they can test or remove elements without causing evaluation errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: GetWithDefault
rubrics_metrics.description: GetWithDefault(list, n, default) returns the nth element if bound, and default otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for weak pointer lists where elements may change. To distinguish unbound vs default-in-list, supply a fresh mutable default (e.g., a newly created string) and use IsIdenticalObj for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbind (delete list entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbind(list[, n]) deletes the element with index n in the mutable list, leaving it unbound (a hole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not an error to unbind a nonexistent list element. IsBound and Unbind do not evaluate their argument to avoid errors when testing or removing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity vs Equality of lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lists are identical if changing one by a list assignment also changes the other (i.e., they are two names for the same object); identity is a refinement of equality. IsIdenticalObj detects identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List literals create new lists not identical to others even if equal. Assigning a list to another variable creates identity. Passing/returning lists preserves identity. Examples illustrate when lists are identical and how mutation affects all names.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShallowCopy semantics for lists
rubrics_metrics.description: ShallowCopy(list) returns a new mutable list not identical to any other list whose elements are identical to the elements of the original list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifying the shallow copy by assignment does not modify the original. Pseudo-code and examples illustrate element identity preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: StructuralCopy semantics for lists
rubrics_metrics.description: StructuralCopy(list) returns a new mutable list whose elements are structural copies (recursively) of the elements of the original list; mutable subobjects are copied (new) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original contains the same mutable object twice, the copy preserves the graph structure by copying that object once and reusing it, i.e., shared subobjects remain shared in the copy. Modifying the structural copy does not affect the original; examples illustrate behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership test for lists (in operator)
rubrics_metrics.description: obj in list tests whether there exists a positive integer i such that list[i] = obj holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list is known to be strictly sorted (IsSSortedList), membership uses binary search and is much quicker than linear search. Examples show difference in number of comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarging internally represented lists (allocation strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a list is enlarged by assignment beyond its end, internally represented lists are enlarged by at least length/8 + 4 entries to avoid frequent reallocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amortized growth strategy reduces the number of enlargements when building lists by repeated assignment. The logical length is stored separately from physical allocation to keep Length efficient. Functions EmptyPlist(len) and ShrinkAllocationPlist(l) allow manual control of allocated space.

rubrics_metrics.name: EmptyPlist and ShrinkAllocationPlist (allocation helpers)
rubrics_metrics.description: EmptyPlist(len) returns an empty plain list preallocated for len entries. ShrinkAllocationPlist(l) returns unused physical memory from l to the memory manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for performance tuning: preallocate if you know final size, shrink to release unused allocated memory. Analogues exist for strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of lists (list comparisons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lists list1 and list2 are equal iff for every index i either both entries are unbound or both are bound and equal (list1[i] = list2[i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality can be problematic for lists containing themselves (may lead to infinite recursion). Examples illustrate equal and unequal lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexicographic ordering of lists
rubrics_metrics.description: list1 < list2 (and <=) order lists lexicographically: find smallest index i where they differ; unbound entries are smaller than any bound entry; then comparison of entries determines ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For < or <= the relevant list elements must themselves be comparable with <; comparing lists with other objects depends on families of elements. Examples illustrate ordering behaviors with holes and different lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic behaviour of lists controlled by filters/categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The arithmetic behaviour (additive and multiplicative) of lists is controlled by categories and attributes (see 21.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows different list-like objects (e.g., ordinary matrices, Lie matrices) to expose different arithmetic semantics while still being lists. Subsequent sections define return values and mutability for arithmetic operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGeneralizedRowVector category
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGeneralizedRowVector(list): true indicates additive arithmetic behaviour of list is as defined in 21.13 and that NestingDepthA attribute will return a nonzero value for list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify lists that behave like (generalized) row vectors under addition. Examples show IsList("abc") vs IsGeneralizedRowVector("abc").

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMultiplicativeGeneralizedRowVector category
rubrics_metrics.description: IsMultiplicativeGeneralizedRowVector(list): true indicates multiplicative arithmetic behaviour of list is as defined in 21.14 and NestingDepthM attribute will return a nonzero value for list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify lists that can be multiplied (e.g., bases in row spaces). Examples illustrate usage.
